::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

:::{#sol-square-of-a-sum}

No:

$$
\begin{aligned}
(3 + 4)^2 &= 7^2 \\
&= 49,
\end{aligned}
$$

while

$$
\begin{aligned}
3^2 + 4^2 &= 9 + 16 \\
&= 25.
\end{aligned}
$$

The difference, $49 - 25 = 24$, is $2 \cdot 3 \cdot 4$.

To see where that extra term comes from,
write the square as a product
and apply the distributive law (@thm-mult-distr) twice:

$$
\ba
(a + b)^2
&= (a + b)(a + b)
&& \text{(definition of a square)}
\\ &= (a + b)\,a + (a + b)\,b
&& \text{(distributive law)}
\\ &= (a^2 + ba) + (ab + b^2)
&& \text{(distributive law, twice)}
\\ &= a^2 + ab + ab + b^2
&& \text{(commutative and associative laws)}
\\ &= a^2 + 2ab + b^2
&& \text{(collect like terms, @def-like-terms)}
\ea
$$

The step "commutative and associative laws" uses @thm-prod-symmetric
to write $ba$ as $ab$,
and @thm-sum-assoc to drop the parentheses.

:::

:::
